title: The New Creation: Regarding No One According to the Flesh
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Watershed of Conversion
subpoints: Conversion changes the direction of life, not just its appearance
Like crossing the continental divide, the destination changes from self to Christ
The change is immediate and total, affecting every aspect of existence

outline.title: Defining 'According to the Flesh'
subpoints: Not merely physical vs. spiritual, but the sinful nature
Not based on ethnic identity or physical appearance
Refers to the natural inclination to rebel and live for self

outline.title: The Two Categories of Christian Living
subpoints: Love for God with all one's being
Faith enables believers to fulfill these duties through the Spirit's change

outline.title: Unbelievers' Relationship to Jesus
subpoints: Seeking power and miracles rather than the Person
Viewing Jesus as merely a prophet or miracle worker

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores the transformative reality of being 'in Christ' as described in 2 Corinthians 5:16-17. Using the analogy of the Lewis and Clark expedition crossing the continental divide, the message illustrates how conversion fundamentally alters the direction of a believer's life. Just as rivers change their destination after crossing the divide, a Christian's life is no longer flowing toward self-fulfillment but toward conformity to the image of Jesus Christ. This change is not merely external but involves a complete reorientation of the heart and purpose.

The sermon addresses the phrase 'according to the flesh,' clarifying that it does not refer to physical bodies, ethnic identity, or appearance, but rather to the sinful nature inherited from Adam. Paul’s assertion that believers no longer regard anyone according to the flesh means that the old, self-centered inclination is dead. Instead, believers relate to God and others through the new reality of being created in Christ, empowered by the Holy Spirit to love God and neighbor genuinely.

Finally, the message contrasts the believer's new relationship with Christ with the typical unbeliever's approach. While unbelievers may view Jesus with curiosity, seek His power for personal gain, or relegate Him to the status of a prophet, the believer knows Him as Lord and Savior. This distinction highlights the necessity of the Spirit's work in changing the heart, enabling a life characterized by authentic love and obedience rather than superficial or self-serving religion.
